chapter: City bands, Johnny Dodds and the bag factory
title: Working with Johnny Dodds, clarinetist, and his drummer brother
summary: Robinson says he and Johnny Dodds worked together and Dodds carried his clarinet to jobs while Robinson still played violin.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Sidney Bechet: the man, the horn, the legend

blocks.x: Yeah, yeah. And that pulled, but that pulled from the metal joint. It broke right there. Yeah. And so he was the fella by the name of Benny. He was to send it back. I don't know all them old boys, but me and Joe Dart, we used to work together. Pretty good how you are, Bart? Thank you, thank you. Me and Joe Dart used to work together. The clarinetist. The clarinetist. Was his name, was it Johnny Dodds or what? Yeah, Joe, he used to call him Joe. Joe. Well, he used to go on the job with his clarinet. He and them used to go together.
He's the one you say his brother was the drummer. Drummer, yeah.
The fellow, yeah. The younger one.

The drummer. Well, I used to work with him. He used to come on the job with his clarinet. I said, man, you're packing that thing all around. But were you playing a clarinet at that time? No, no. No, you were still with the violin. Yeah, yeah. I never did bother with it that time. But I just pick up on it, you know, all of a sudden, like a harmonica. Any devilish thing I put my hand on. I got a harmonica for, I don't know how long. I got two in there.
